units.function: Shared runtime substrate for local, SSH and sandbox execution: process lifecycle, ACPX, sessions, workspace transfer, managed runtimes, callback bridge, env shaping, redaction, skills, billing and transcript types.
units.dependencyDirection: All first-party Agent adapters depend inward on this package; it depends on `acpx` and `picocolors`, while also carrying server, CLI and UI-facing types. Server core imports it directly.
units.keyDataModels: AdapterAgent, AdapterRuntime, AdapterExecutionContext/Result, execution targets, session codec/compaction, runtime services, skill snapshots, transcript entries and callback bridge requests.
units.lifecycle: Prepare workspace/runtime → shape environment and credentials → spawn or resume process/session → stream logs/events → collect usage/result → restore workspace → terminate/clean up. Remote and sandbox paths add transfer and bridge leases.
units.testAssessment: 22 focused tests cover process, SSH, sandbox confinement, sync/restore, MCP isolation, callback authorization, redaction and session behavior. Large `server-utils.ts` and ~3,800-line ACPX executor still concentrate many coupled branches and integration assumptions.
units.designRationale: Normalize heterogeneous CLI/ACP runtimes and prevent each provider adapter from reimplementing transport, process and workspace safety.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equal Connector lifecycle, remote/local execution nodes, fencing, cancellation, timeout, evidence, workspace/data egress and secret-safe runtime proof.
units.companyOsFit: Many invariants are valuable, but the contract mixes Paperclip issue/heartbeat vocabulary, raw auth token injection, provider sessions, UI transcript types and transport implementation. It is not a neutral Company OS Connector SDK.
units.responsibilityConflict: ExecutionContext carries authority as an optional raw `authToken`, while permission bypass and tool actions are adapter concerns; Company OS requires action-digest approval and accountable-human responsibility before any capability lease is issued.

units.function: Documents and tests the no-remote-git persistence contract for adapters.
units.dependencyDirection: Constrains adapters, adapter-utils, server and CLI; static CI rejects unapproved `git push` paths.
units.keyDataModels: Execution workspace, transported copy, remote URL metadata and finalize status.
units.lifecycle: Local worktree is authoritative across runs; remote copies sync out and back, and failed restoration blocks dependent work.
units.testAssessment: A fixture test proves remote-only commits return without any configured remote; a static source scan enforces the policy with reasoned exceptions.
units.designRationale: Avoid hidden dependence on credentials, remotes or branch publication for cross-run durability.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS execution nodes need an explicit durable-state owner and must distinguish work persistence from external publication.
units.companyOsFit: Strongly aligned. Company OS should generalize it to an Artifact/WorkspacePort and require publication as a separately approved action.
units.responsibilityConflict: Implicit `git push` would be an unapproved external side effect; the ban supports Company OS responsibility semantics.

units.function: Runs Claude Code through CLI or ACP, with model/quota discovery, config/skill materialization, local/remote execution and transcript parsing.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils and Claude ACP; imported directly by server and UI, so provider details cross backend/frontend boundaries.
units.keyDataModels: Provider config, ACP session, model profile, quota windows, skill snapshot and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Auto-select ACP or CLI → materialize config/skills → probe auth/model → execute/resume → parse output/usage → preserve session and workspace.
units.testAssessment: Eight focused tests cover ACP fallback, remote execution, permissions, parsing, config and probes. Credential/config materialization and host-provider calls remain sensitive integration surfaces.
units.designRationale: Offer one adapter despite two execution engines and several Claude authentication modes.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral engine negotiation and runtime health without losing provider-specific capabilities.
units.companyOsFit: Engine fallback and remote permission narrowing are useful patterns; direct code is coupled to Paperclip env, prompt and session semantics.
units.responsibilityConflict: `dangerouslySkipPermissions` defaults true and local confinement is off by default. Company OS must never treat provider bypass flags as organizational approval.

units.function: Runs Codex by CLI or ACP with model profiles, output/process inactivity monitoring, isolated homes, device login and identity-keyed credential cache/copyback.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils and Codex ACP; server and UI import provider constants, schemas, parsers and execution hooks.
units.keyDataModels: Codex session, managed CODEX_HOME, subscription account identity, cached credential version, device-login transcript and runtime config.
units.lifecycle: Resolve engine/home/auth precedence → optionally vend only a newer same-identity credential → execute with activity monitor → parse usage/session → merge credential updates under lock → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: 26 tests are the strongest adapter suite and cover auth precedence, path/symlink safety, copyback races, device-login parsing, activity monitoring, remote execution and output parsing.
units.designRationale: Keep long-lived subscription credentials usable across isolated runs without cross-company or cross-account credential substitution.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS had not yet fully specified identity-anchored credential refresh/copyback, silent-process liveness or auth-format migration.
units.companyOsFit: These are important requirements to add to Secret/Execution ports; implementation remains Codex/Paperclip filesystem and auth-format specific.
units.responsibilityConflict: The adapter exposes a bypass-approvals/sandbox default and must not equate CLI device identity with accountable enterprise human authority.

units.function: Invokes durable Cursor Cloud Agents through the vendor SDK and maps Paperclip heartbeats to remote runs.
units.dependencyDirection: Direct vendor SDK dependency; server passes issue/run context and a minted Paperclip token into the remote environment.
units.keyDataModels: Repository/runtime identity, durable Cursor agent session, remote run attachment, vendor API key and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Validate vendor config → create or reattach durable remote agent → inject scoped run environment → wait/poll remote run → preserve session identity.
units.testAssessment: Four tests cover execution, session identity and UI parsing; actual vendor failure, cancellation, billing and data-residency paths need live-contract tests.
units.designRationale: Let the vendor own remote code execution while Paperclip retains task state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs external managed-runtime connectors with explicit residency, cancellation, timeout, evidence and exit semantics.
units.companyOsFit: The ownership split is useful, but vendor session and token injection must stay inside a Connector adapter and local execution node.
units.responsibilityConflict: A remote vendor run can act on a repository; Company OS must bind the exact repository/data/action scope to a responsibility contract and approval digest.

units.function: Runs Cursor Agent CLI locally or remotely with session resume, stream parsing, skills and trust controls.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; vendor CLI installation uses an unpinned remote installer and execution results flow into server/UI parsers.
units.keyDataModels: Cursor session/cwd identity, model profile, stream events and remote command.
units.lifecycle: Resolve command/model → transport workspace if remote → execute/resume session → parse stream → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: Four tests cover local/remote execution and command selection; installer provenance, credential isolation and cancellation receive limited direct coverage.
units.designRationale: Normalize Cursor's local CLI despite the lack of a registry-distributed installer artifact.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs an install provenance policy for execution-node tooling.
units.companyOsFit: Runtime shape is ordinary Connector adapter work; unpinned `curl | bash` is not acceptable for enterprise production.
units.responsibilityConflict: Tool installation and repository writes are separate high-risk actions and cannot inherit work approval automatically.

units.function: Runs Gemini CLI through ACP or CLI with fallback, session parsing, remote execution and skill materialization.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; provider-specific config and transcript modules are imported by server and UI.
units.keyDataModels: Gemini ACP/CLI session, provider config, skill snapshot and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Check ACP prerequisites/version → choose engine → stage config/skills/workspace → execute → parse/resume → restore.
units.testAssessment: Six focused tests cover ACP, fallback, remote behavior, parsing and UI config; vendor auth and quota contracts are mostly probe-driven.
units.designRationale: Mask Gemini CLI version and ACP capability variation behind one adapter.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector negotiation must express optional engine versions and deterministic fallback without changing work identity.
units.companyOsFit: Capability negotiation is useful; implementation and session details remain vendor-specific.
units.responsibilityConflict: Fallback must not silently change sandbox or permission guarantees; Company OS must attest the actual engine and confinement used.

units.function: Runs Grok CLI as a single-turn/session-resumable coding Agent and normalizes turn boundaries and transcripts.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; workspace skills and provider stream formats flow to server/UI.
units.keyDataModels: Session ID/cwd, streaming turn boundary, tool/result transcript and runtime skill set.
units.lifecycle: Stage project skills → execute or resume → recognize provider turn boundaries → capture result/session → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: Seven tests emphasize parsers, turn boundaries, config and environment probes; remote and security coverage is thinner than Codex/Claude.
units.designRationale: Prevent provider stream quirks from leaking into core run state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs connector conformance tests for progress/result ordering and duplicate terminal events.
units.companyOsFit: Parser lessons are relevant, but no generic code should be copied into core.
units.responsibilityConflict: Provider turn completion is not Company OS work completion; evidence and responsibility projections must decide terminal state.

units.function: Provides local and gateway Hermes adapters plus an Agent-facing task-bridge skill that can call Paperclip REST APIs.
units.dependencyDirection: Local execution depends on adapter-utils; gateway and task bridge add outbound HTTP and Paperclip credential semantics within the same distributable package.
units.keyDataModels: Hermes session, provider/model config, gateway transport, task-bridge scope and API key.
units.lifecycle: Detect local configuration or gateway → execute/resume → parse output; independently, the task bridge reads a scoped API key and mutates tasks.
units.testAssessment: Eight tests cover execution spawn, command/model resolution, prompt rendering, bridge scope and UI parsing. Gateway and internet-facing bridge require stronger adversarial/E2E coverage.
units.designRationale: Support Hermes as both a managed employee and an external entry point into task management.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs to separate execution connectors from inbound delegated-control connectors and give each distinct scopes/audiences.
units.companyOsFit: The package demonstrates the danger of combining these roles. Company OS should define separate Connector profiles and credentials.
units.responsibilityConflict: Agent-originated task mutation can create goals or delegation; it must identify the human sponsor and cannot use a normal execution credential.

units.function: Compatibility/re-export shim exposing the gateway implementation from the Hermes package.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends entirely on `@paperclipai/hermes-paperclip-adapter`; contains no independent runtime logic.
units.keyDataModels: None beyond re-exported Hermes gateway types.
units.lifecycle: Built and published as a separate package wrapper; behavior changes whenever the underlying Hermes package changes.
units.testAssessment: No package-local tests; confidence is indirect through the underlying package.
units.designRationale: Preserve package naming/compatibility while consolidating implementation.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS may eventually need deprecation shims for Connector packages.
units.companyOsFit: No current need and no reusable implementation.

units.function: Connects to OpenClaw over WebSocket, performs gateway/device authentication, optional auto-pairing, session routing and wake/result normalization.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils and `ws`; adapter config may contain shared tokens/passwords and defaults to broad `operator.admin` scopes.
units.keyDataModels: Gateway connection challenge, device identity, shared auth, scopes, session key strategy, wait request and normalized runtime service reports.
units.lifecycle: Resolve credentials/device → open/challenge/connect → optionally approve pairing → send Agent request → wait/stream → normalize result → close or retain session route.
units.testAssessment: Two large tests cover execution protocol and UI config, but broad scopes, first-connect auto-approval and reconnect/cancel races warrant dedicated security/property tests.
units.designRationale: Integrate a remote Agent runtime whose native protocol has its own pairing and session semantics.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs connector bootstrap/pairing, capability attenuation, revocation, reconnect and remote identity proof.
units.companyOsFit: The problem is important; the Paperclip/OpenClaw wire implementation must remain adapter-specific and credentials must be secret references.
units.responsibilityConflict: Default `operator.admin` and automatic pairing are incompatible with least privilege unless a human approves the exact connector enrollment and capability set.

units.function: Runs OpenCode CLI with multi-provider model discovery, session resume, runtime config/skills and optional remote sandbox execution.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; installer executes an unpinned remote script and server expands credential placeholders into provider config.
units.keyDataModels: Provider/model ID, session/cwd, generated opencode config, skill set and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Install/probe → discover model → generate runtime config with resolved refs → execute/resume → parse result → restore workspace.
units.testAssessment: Seven tests cover execution, remote path, models, parsing and runtime config; installer integrity and generated-secret cleanup are not equivalent to a full threat-model test.
units.designRationale: Support a provider-agnostic Agent CLI and avoid installing several unused architecture binaries.
units.companyOsProblem: Execution nodes need signed/pinned tool acquisition and ephemeral secret materialization with destruction proof.
units.companyOsFit: Multi-provider selection belongs above the adapter, but unverified `curl | bash`, permission bypass default and secret-bearing generated files conflict with enterprise defaults.
units.responsibilityConflict: External-directory permission defaults true; generated provider credentials can outlive the approved action unless lease cleanup is proven.

units.function: Runs Pi coding Agent with provider/model discovery, sessions, skills and generated provider runtime configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: Depends on adapter-utils; provider secret placeholders are resolved server-side into configuration shipped to local or remote execution.
units.keyDataModels: Provider/model, thinking level, session/cwd, models.json/provider config, skill snapshot and execution result.
units.lifecycle: Probe pinned npm CLI → discover/validate model → materialize provider config/skills → execute/resume → parse → restore.
units.testAssessment: Four tests cover remote execution, models, parser and runtime config; cleanup, cancellation and secret residue need stronger tests.
units.designRationale: Expose Pi's multi-provider tool runtime through the same adapter surface.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs provider-neutral model routing while keeping credentials inside the execution plane.
units.companyOsFit: Pinned installer is better than remote script, but direct provider config materialization stays an adapter implementation detail.
units.responsibilityConflict: All tools are enabled by default; Company OS capability leases and data egress policy must constrain the actual tool set per work action.
